assumptions: The offer is still at planning and pre-validation stage, with no paid customers, repeat purchases, committed channel partners, or demonstrated release-decision impact beyond the supplied evidence.

The commercial offer remains one fixed PPG motion-stress gate for one device-algorithm version, sold up front for 8000-20000 PLN without subscription revenue, certification claims, or bundled participant collection.

The founder can automate much of the analysis and reporting within a 15-20 hour weekly commitment, while privacy, regulatory, legal, and any participant-facing work is contracted within the stated 80000 PLN capital envelope.

Public datasets and synthetic artefacts are sufficient to build a credible pilot protocol, but customer traces and reusable derived failure features are used only when contracts and applicable data-protection controls permit them.
The number of reachable small PPG teams, their release frequency, and the share that outsource an independent gate are unknown rather than assumed to be either large or negligible.

The opportunity is assessed as competently executed with extensive AI leverage, while trust, regulatory expertise, customer access, and lawful data rights still require human or institutional capability.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Motion and activity materially alter wrist-PPG error, while a release freeze creates a concrete moment when an independent, context-specific check can be useful. Turning that need into a narrow pass/fail gate is coherent, though the underlying need for device-specific validation is already understood by regulators, engineering teams, and validation-tool vendors rather than being a hidden market truth.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A missed motion-related defect can compromise a release or study dataset, giving the buyer a rational reason to pay for credible independent testing. However, the supplied evidence does not establish that small teams view this narrow external gate as urgent, control a budget at release freeze, or will pay 8000-20000 PLN instead of using internal QA, public datasets, platforms, or simulators; those are consequential unknowns, not proof of no demand.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Up-front payment, fixed scope, and protocol reuse support cash conversion and could produce respectable service margins without large initial investment. The central economics remain unresolved: delivery hours, specialist costs, CAC, gross margin, price realization, repurchase frequency, and customer value are unmeasured, while per-release project revenue lacks the retained revenue and operating leverage needed to make the founder's wealth path credible at present.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Small wrist-wearable and PPG algorithm teams approaching a version release form a sharply defined and operationally reachable beachhead. That precision aids testing, but no supplied evidence establishes enough qualified teams, sufficiently frequent releases, or enough outsourced-validation spend for this narrow segment to be economically meaningful beyond a specialist consultancy.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A trusted neutral report placed directly in the release workflow could become the default gate for a small niche. Today the offer has no accreditation, embedded channel, proprietary corpus, switching cost, or demonstrated decision superiority, while capable buyers and established platforms or simulator vendors can cover substantial portions of the job, making niche domination possible but presently weakly supported.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Successful PPG gates could lead to additional motion protocols, modalities, device classes, geographies, or a licensed failure-signature product. Expansion is not automatic because validation remains context-, population-, and intended-purpose-specific, so each adjacency may require new evidence, expertise, data rights, and buyer trust rather than inheriting the full economics of the first protocol.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Versioned protocols, decision templates, accumulated reputation, and lawfully reusable derived failure signatures could compound with repeated audits. The prospective data asset depends on permissions customers may refuse, while public datasets, published methods, and a reproducible fixed protocol leave the initial service readily imitable and provide limited protection from price pressure.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer is narrower and potentially more decision-focused than a generic data audit, and independence may matter when an internal team is close to release. There is no evidence yet that it catches materially different failures, saves enough engineering time, shortens release cycles, or delivers greater trust than lower-priced audits, public-data workflows, research platforms, or dedicated validation hardware.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Regulatory attention to fit-for-purpose digital measurements, ongoing wearable algorithm iteration, and documented activity-dependent error create a favorable reason to test the offer now. The same maturity has also produced established tools and sophisticated internal practices, and the gate cannot substitute for purpose-specific clinical or regulatory validation, so timing helps demand without creating a uniquely open window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A public sample protocol and bounded technical outreach provide a plausible low-cost route to early conversations in a specialist market. No CRO or regulatory-consultant relationship is committed, no conversion or CAC evidence exists, and direct selling to a small dispersed buyer set may remain founder-intensive; repeatable partner-led acquisition is therefore a hypothesis rather than an established channel.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The narrow protocol fits the founder's biosignal, neuroscience, data-science, automation, capital, and part-time constraints materially better than a broad laboratory or platform. A pilot is feasible, but commercial credibility, qualified regulatory boundaries, GDPR-compliant trace handling, contracts for derived-data reuse, and strict avoidance of implied certification remain meaningful execution requirements that AI cannot eliminate.

main_structural_strength: The offer is tied to a precise, high-consequence release event and compresses a technically credible PPG motion problem into one up-front, repeatable gate that strongly matches the founder's expertise and part-time constraints.
primary_score_limiter: The combination of an unproven narrow buyer pool, project-based revenue, uncertain repeat frequency, and unvalidated acquisition leaves no credible route yet from a useful specialist audit to scalable owner earnings or a dominant position.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Adjacent buyers can already access a Labfront audit starting at USD 500, established research platforms and ECG/PPG simulators, plus openly licensed reference-labelled datasets, showing both a materially lower price anchor and credible build-or-buy substitutes for a standalone gate.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots from multiple independent PPG teams at the proposed price, measured delivery margin and acquisition effort, documented cases where the gate changes a release decision or saves meaningful validation time, at least two later-version repurchases, a repeatable qualified-introduction channel, and signed terms permitting lawful reuse of derived failure features would materially improve the judgment.
highest_value_structural_change: Make the gate an embedded white-label step in a specialist CRO or regulatory-consultant release workflow under a minimum-volume commercial agreement, with explicit derived-feature reuse rights and standardized handoff data; this would jointly strengthen trust, distribution, repeat frequency, and the compounding asset rather than relying on one-off founder-led audit sales.
